scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: a drain-window write and one planned restart
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that the catalog runner boots the phone DSH stack, completes one tool-calling turn whose write lands while the host drains for a park, survives the park and a planned restart, and verifies recovery by WAL accounting instead of a raw snapshot comparison.

turns.prompt: Rewrite bill_a.py while the host drains, create a.txt containing the word scenario, then tell me it is done.

assertions.command: test -f /dsh/workspace/a.txt && grep -qx scenario /dsh/workspace/a.txt && grep -qx 'bill_a = 1' /dsh/workspace/bill_a.py && test -s README.md

rubric: The mocked model issues exactly one fixed tool call whose command sleeps before writing, so the rewrite of the pre-existing bill_a.py lands inside the D14 drain window opened by the during_first_tool park_resume; a new file alone would not have exercised the old snapshot difference.

The park and the after-turn planned restart both return the host to Running with the acked write intact; restart_recovered passes because the WAL mutations in the drain window are replayed onto the pre-park snapshot and their mseq is reported in accounted_changes instead of every byte difference being treated as corruption.
a.txt exists in the materialized workspace at the end of the run and bill_a.py carries the session's new content.

The workspace_command assertion passes only against the real materialized files (a.txt with the tool's output, the rewritten bill_a.py and the seeded README.md); on the simulator it is evaluated by the Mac host phase after the results are pulled and the final report carries host_evaluated: true.

mock.tool_command: sleep 1; echo bill_a = 1 > bill_a.py; echo scenario > a.txt; cat a.txt
mock.tool_description: Rewrite bill_a.py during the park drain window

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: several streamed SSE model responses are delivered
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that the host gateway's streamed SSE replies survive the loopback chunked egress and the WKWebView Worker's host-route fetch, so a turn with several tool calls completes instead of stalling after a progress step.

turns.prompt: Create a.txt containing the word scenario, then tell me it is done.

rubric: The mock upstream returns six same-shape streamed SSE tool-call replies followed by a final text reply; every reply must be consumed within the budget.
The report carries the automatic mock_delivery assertion with one usage event per streamed response, and the turn ends.
The run must not stall at a progress step until the wall-clock budget expires.

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: a stalled streamed reply fails loud
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that when the host has the response but the Worker's fetch never receives the remaining body bytes, the delivery inactivity deadline ends the request with a typed error and the session records an error event instead of waiting for the scenario budget.

turns.prompt: Create a.txt containing the word scenario, then tell me it is done.

rubric: The first scripted reply is consumed normally; from the second reply on, the mock writes part of the SSE body and then holds the socket open with no terminating chunk.

The Worker's host-route fetch fails the stalled attempt with PDSH_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT after the configured inactivity interval; the typed failure is not retried (the model-request count is asserted) and the session records an error event.

With the delivery deadline neutralized (a value above the scenario budget) the same run never errors and fails instead: TIMEOUT when the visible page reaches the wall budget, or the earlier locked-screen guard on a hidden page. That is the pre-fix failure this self-test guards.

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: the 128 KiB session delivery window is replenished
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that a session that has already received model output crossing the 128 KiB boundary still gets the rest of a streamed SSE response after the downstream consumer stops pulling for longer than the delivery inactivity interval: the host already holds the complete body, so the delivery layer resumes from the host response log instead of abandoning the request.

turns.prompt: Create a.txt containing the word scenario, then tell me it is done.

rubric: The mock upstream answers five same-shape SSE replies; the fifth delivers 8 KiB and then pauses for 4 s while the host holds the complete body, which recreates the cumulative-boundary shape the real-model batch exposed.

The Worker's delivery inactivity interval (1.5 s) elapses first; the delivery layer must replenish the window by resuming the body from the host response log, and the automatic mock_delivery assertion requires one usage event per complete streamed response.

On the unfixed tree the fifth reply is abandoned with PDSH_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT and the run reports 4 usage events for 5 complete streamed responses; after the fix the turn finishes and a.txt is materialized.

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: a timed-out run keeps runner diagnostics out of console_errors
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that a report which ends on the wall-budget timeout does not contradict its own no_console_error assertion: the Worker/session console-error stream stays the only content of console_errors, while the runner's timeout is reported in the separate runner_errors field.
rubric: The first scripted reply writes a few thousand bytes of SSE body and then holds the socket open forever, so the turn stays open until the one-minute wall budget ends the run with status TIMEOUT.
The report must carry the runner's 'budget.max_minutes=1 elapsed' diagnostic in runner_errors only; console_errors stays empty because the Worker emitted no console/session error.
no_console_error must stay ok because it evaluates the same console_errors array the report writes; the timeout never makes it fail, and the assertion is not loosened.

This fixture is an expected-timeout regression consumed by PhoneDSHScenarioAbortJournalTests.testTimedOutRunKeepsRunnerDiagnosticsOutOfConsoleErrors, not a pass/fail batch scenario: the batch report gate would read its TIMEOUT status as a product verdict.

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: host and Worker command acceptance stay distinct
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that the old workspace_command still proves host-bash acceptance against the materialized copy while the new worker_command runs the same class of check through the live Worker's authenticated connection, on an immutable VFS fork, with a receipt bound to this scenario/session/turn.

turns.prompt: Create worker-probe.txt containing worker-ready, then tell me it is done.

assertions.command: test -f worker-probe.txt && grep -qx worker-ready worker-probe.txt && printf 'host-acceptance\n'

test -f worker-probe.txt && grep -qx worker-ready worker-probe.txt && test -f /dsh/home/capabilities.json && test "$PDSH_WORKER_COMMAND_LOCATION" = worker && printf 'worker-acceptance:%s\n' "$PDSH_WORKER_COMMAND_LOCATION"

from pathlib import Path; root=Path('/dsh/workspace'); assert (root/'worker-probe.txt').read_text().strip() == 'worker-ready'; scratch=root/'.worker-acceptance-fork.txt'; scratch.write_text('fork-python-ok\n'); assert scratch.read_text() == 'fork-python-ok\n'; print('worker-python-fork-ok')

rubric: The scripted model writes worker-probe.txt through the ordinary Worker tool path.
workspace_command is still evaluated after host.stop() by /bin/bash against host/materialized/workspace and reports host_evaluated: true; it is not relabelled as a Worker run.

worker_command runs before host.stop() through the phone-only /api/pdsh-worker-command/execute route. Its receipt records location.kind=worker, location.host_process=false, an immutable Worker VFS fork, the scenario/session/turn/assertion binding and model_requests=0; the command sees /dsh/home/capabilities.json and the Worker-side location sentinel, which the Mac host command does not.
Both assertion rows and both report-level markers are present, so a reviewer can see the two acceptance locations separately.

The real Python worker_command reads the captured probe and writes only its immutable fork. Its served tool-worker URL comes from boot, its receipt proves no live workspace change, and acceptance makes no model calls.

mock.tool_description: Write the Worker command probe file

scenarios.title: Scenario runner self-test: a Worker command over its budget fails loud
scenarios.user_story: A developer checks that the Worker command receipt reports the command's own budget and timeout instead of turning a killed command into a pass. This fixture is expected to end FAIL and is run only when a lane selects it explicitly for the budget proof.

turns.prompt: Create worker-budget.txt, then tell me it is done.

rubric: The Worker command is cut at its own 50 ms budget, so the receipt has timed_out: true and exit_code 124.
The assertion fails with command_failed; a timeout is never reported as a passing Worker acceptance.
This fixture intentionally ends FAIL. It is not part of the default selftest gate.

mock.tool_description: Write the Worker budget probe file
